content: Melvin-Koushki says Ibn Turka elsewhere contrasts the object of lettrism with the philosophical concept of absolute existence (al-wujūd al-muṭlaq), the focus of his Tamhīd al-Qawāʿid: because it is relevant only to things that exist, it cannot be the object of a universal science. Only the letter encompasses all that is and is not, all that can and cannot be; it alone is the coincidentia oppositorum.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, K. al-Mafāḥiṣ; Tamhīd al-Qawāʿid
